name: test2
note: harder shapes — a 2-D interaction invisible at 1-D, a ramp-in rather than a step, and a sub-floor global dip that must stay silent.

incidents.why: Simpson's case: -50% inside a 9.6%-of-traffic cell dilutes to -16.1% at region=EU and -13.2% at os_version=Android 14 (measured). Both 1-D views must be ruled out in favour of the cross-cut, and peeling the cell out must leave each with a ~0% residual.
demand-side price drop in one app category; baseline days overlap T2-1's window, so it also exercises contamination exclusion.
gradual degradation (-11.7% / -23.3% / -35%) rather than a step — a step-only detector clips the window.

-2% everywhere is under the 5% relative floor for ratio metrics. Firing on it is noise, not an incident. Measured cell-level eCPM noise on a clean slice is p99 1.9% / max 4.3%, so -4% sat too close to the floor to be a stable control; -2% leaves real headroom.
CTR halves in the largest APAC market and revenue does not move a cent — this is a CPM model, clicks buy nothing. Scope is revenue via fill_rate + eCPM, so firing here is fabricating an incident.
